newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara tenders for deposit as rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara tenders for deposit as rates fall.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia issued a tender on Friday calling for a one-month deposit as part of its open market intervention operation.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the domestic money market to keep liquidity under check or set interest rates.
Dealers said a continuous fall in interest rates this week despite a large outgo of funds from the system on Monday had attracted central bank intervention.
Banks paid out two billion ringgit for a seven-year government bond issue and also topped up their statutory reserve accounts with the central bank on Monday.
But dealers said financial institutions had covered excessively for the bond issue and overseas funds were making a comeback to the Malaysian market, which had kept rates under pressure.
Ahead of the tender, one one-week money was at 6.40/50 percent, two-week at 6.70/80 and one-month at 7.10/15, all steady at Thursday's levels.
Three-month money was unchanged at 7.20/25 percent against 7.25/30, while six-month was steady at 7.25/30.
